title: Asset Library
subtitle: Market-proven logo and app-icon design styles. Every style comes with a breakdown of real commercial cases (where the look comes from and why it works) plus a copy-ready AI image prompt — drop in your brand name and go.

styles.name: Solid Glyph
styles.tagline: One flat color, one symbol — still readable at 16px
styles.intro: A single background color and one high-contrast symbol: no gradients, no text. This is the most noise-proof move in an icon ocean — among dozens of App Store icons, a solid block plus a simple shape is read in 0.1 seconds. Spotify green, Things orange, Claude cream: the color itself is the entry point.
why: Color asset: keep one exclusive hue and users find you by scanning
Never smudges at tiny sizes: few strokes means notification bar, watch and dark mode all work
Merch-friendly: a clean color block on any backdrop, zero-cost marketing art
Constraint: the hue must be near-exclusive — a color clash means sharing traffic

cases.note: Black sound-wave arcs on green; only the stroke weight has ever been tweaked, and the 'green = music' grip has never been taken.
One white arrow on orange — a paid productivity tool dares to use a toy-bright color because the glyph is absolutely simple.
An orange starburst on cream: while every AI product went dark, the warm hand-drawn feel became the identifier.

styles.prompt: Design an app icon for {{APP_NAME}}: one flat solid background ({{COLOR_1}}), one high-contrast centered glyph ({{COLOR_2}}), no gradients, no text, no shadows. The glyph must stay legible at 29x29 px. Rounded-square iOS icon format, 1024x1024, generous padding, flat vector style.
styles.promptHint: Pick a {{COLOR_1}} you can own long-term and max out the contrast with {{COLOR_2}}; shrink to 29px and check it still reads.

styles.name: Gradient
styles.tagline: The gradient 'premium feel' is the most validated recipe there is
styles.intro: A colorful gradient base plus a white line glyph — since Instagram this has all but become the uniform of consumer breakout apps. The gradient gives a static icon light and depth while the white foreground keeps the glyph clean. Only To-C products dare saturated gradients — the signal is 'popular, energetic, worth opening'.
why: Free premium: one gradient replaces a whole skeuomorphic highlight stack — the icon instantly costs more
White foreground is lazy-proof: the glyph never has to blend with the base
Works on light and dark wallpapers: gradients carry their own light
Constraint: hue real estate is crowded — avoid the ranges Instagram / Apple Music already own

cases.note: Swapped the skeuomorphic camera for a pink-orange-yellow gradient and within months 'candy' became its unofficial nickname.
A blue-violet gradient sparkle — Google unified its entire AI line under this breathing light effect.
A white note on pink gradient: the most 'neon' tile in Apple's own grid, aimed straight at young music scenes.
A paper plane on blue-cyan gradient, camped opposite WhatsApp green; the gradient gives the plane volume.

styles.prompt: Design an app icon for {{APP_NAME}}: a smooth diagonal gradient background ({{COLOR_1}} to {{COLOR_2}}, optional third hue), a single white outline glyph of {{SUBJECT}} centered, no text, soft light sheen, rounded-square iOS icon format, 1024x1024, flat modern style like a top-charting consumer app.
styles.promptHint: Check your gradient hues aren't already Instagram / Apple Music / Telegram territory; keep the white glyph under three main curves.

styles.name: Lettermark
styles.tagline: One letter fills the screen — even a rename can't dislodge it
styles.intro: Turn the brand's initial into the only graphic: Uber's U, X's X, Netflix's N. The lettermark is the privilege of category-defining platforms — users already know the word, so the icon just repeats it. The letter fills the canvas with almost no ornament: the most confident posture in any list.
why: Zero learning cost: icon and name are the same thing — remembering one remembers the other
Rename-proof: Twitter → X changed only the letter and the whole visual system survived
Composition is inherently stable: one big centered character never smudges
Constraint: for a startup, a lettermark just magnifies a name nobody knows

cases.note: A white U on black, distilled from a busy map glyph to a single letter — the act of restraint was itself the confidence statement.
The Twitter bird retired and the letter X took everything — the largest-ever 'rename without moving the visual center' experiment.
The gradient Bélo on white: one mark that is simultaneously the letter A, a heart, a person and a location pin.
A folded red N on black, film-strip depth built into the strokes — the brand color is the channel color.

styles.prompt: Design an app icon for {{APP_NAME}}: a single bold letter "{{LETTER}}" filling the canvas, custom geometric sans-serif, {{COLOR_1}} background with {{COLOR_2}} letter (or inverted), no extra ornament, the letter may carry one subtle fold or gradient detail, rounded-square iOS icon format, 1024x1024.
styles.promptHint: The letter should span at least 60% of the width to 'fill the screen'; at most one decorative detail, and it must vanish cleanly at 29px.

styles.name: Mascot
styles.tagline: Put the character's face on the icon — the bond forms before the app even opens
styles.intro: A mascot icon fits an expressive character into 1024px: Duolingo's owl, Reddit's Snoo, bilibili's little TV. Characters carry personality and fan-art space; users open the app 'to see what it's doing today' — the favorite weapon of retention-obsessed categories (learning, community, youth culture).
why: Emotional entry: costumes swap with holidays and events — the icon itself becomes content
Memory beats geometry: humans remember faces far better than shapes, it pops out of any list
Social amplifier: sticker packs, merch, animation — the icon is just the starting point
Constraint: once a character lands it's nearly impossible to replace; budget for the IP early

cases.note: Duo the owl permanently headlines the 'scariest study nag' meme — the icon is the marketing, at half budget.
Snoo, the antenna-topped white figure on orange: the whole community vibe rests on that harmless face, barely redrawn for years.
A pink little TV — chassis plus two antennae say 'ACG community' completely.

styles.prompt: Design an app icon for {{APP_NAME}}: a friendly {{CREATURE}} mascot face centered on a {{COLOR_1}} background, big eyes, simple rounded shapes, flat illustration style with soft shading, no text, must stay readable at 29x29 px, rounded-square iOS icon format, 1024x1024.
styles.promptHint: Head only, no full body; bind {{CREATURE}} to the product's temperament (learning = owl, community = little robot) and give the eyes at least a third of the face width.

styles.name: Rich Texture
styles.tagline: A stroke of paint, a sliver of light — an icon built like a small artwork
styles.intro: Real light, paint and material turn the icon into a miniature artwork: Procreate's rainbow brush stroke, Genshin's metal crest. The textured route keeps getting validated in the two experience-heavy categories — creative tools and games: the more the icon looks like a poster, the more users trust the product's quality.
why: Quality signal: brushwork and lighting declare 'this is for people who do serious work'
Instant standout: most of the list is flat color blocks, one textured icon jumps out
Emotional density: games pre-stage their world, tools pay homage to craft
Constraint: detail dies at small sizes — ship a simplified variant for notification bars

cases.note: One wet rainbow stroke on black — the 'sharpen your tools' manifesto compressed into a single brush mark.
A platinum-gradient metal crest: the game's Teyvat worldview rendered as a collectible badge.

styles.prompt: Design an app icon for {{APP_NAME}}: a single dramatic {{TEXTURE_SUBJECT}} (brush stroke / emblem / artifact) with realistic lighting and rich color on a dark {{COLOR_1}} background, poster-quality rendering, centered composition, no text, rounded-square iOS icon format, 1024x1024.
styles.promptHint: Render two versions: the 1024 detail cut and a 29px simplified cut; keep exactly one textured subject — cut the second element.

styles.name: Colorful Geometric
styles.tagline: Three or four colors assembled into one shape — the professional tool uniform
styles.intro: Several saturated blocks assembled into a single mark: Figma's four-color bars, Slack's colored hash, Google Photos' four-color pinwheel. Multicolor geometry is the safest language for collaboration and productivity tools — each color can map to a product module, making the icon a legend for the information architecture.
why: Color as function: icon palette maps one-to-one to the in-app palette, closing the recognition loop
Breaks the serious-tool monotony: professional apps can't be cutesy, but they can be multicolor
Structure that splits: one mark of interlocking parts feeds motion, loaders and brand kits alike
Constraint: hold the palette to 3-5 colors — beyond that it's a paint aisle

cases.note: Four colored rounded bars assemble an outline — the colors of the product panels are the colors of the icon.
A colored hash: the abstract idea of 'channel' drawn directly as four arcs.
A four-color pinwheel — 'photos auto-arranged into albums' rotated into a single shape.

styles.prompt: Design an app icon for {{APP_NAME}}: one unified mark assembled from 3-4 rounded geometric shapes, each in a distinct saturated color ({{COLOR_1}}, {{COLOR_2}}, {{COLOR_3}}, optional {{COLOR_4}}), on a white or very light background, flat vector, precise alignment, no text, rounded-square iOS icon format, 1024x1024.
styles.promptHint: Fix 3-4 HEX values before writing the prompt; the shapes must overlap or interlock — laid out separately they become a swatch strip.

styles.name: Minimal Light
styles.tagline: One blank amid a screen of color steals the show
styles.intro: White background plus a single thin dark glyph — trading away color presence for 'premium and calm': Notion's serifed N, Threads' tangled line. In an ocean of colorful icons, white is contrarianly loud; it also promises the product UI is just as clean — the icon is the trailer for the product's temperament.
why: Contrarian placement: a white block pops hardest on dark wallpapers and turns 'papery' on light ones
Temperament trailer: white plus hairline = restrained, professional, document-like — expectation management for free
Never dates: black on white carries no trend-color risk, no redraw for a decade
Constraint: the glyph must be distinctive, or white-on-black reads as a built-in system app
fits: Professional products after a composed feel

cases.note: A black serifed N on white — one letter that borrows the entire 'paper and pen' tradition.
A single tangled curve on white: Meta's way of drawing a line from Instagram's rainbow gradient.

styles.prompt: Design an app icon for {{APP_NAME}}: pure white background, one thin elegant {{COLOR_1}} glyph of {{SUBJECT}} (single continuous line preferred), generous negative space, editorial minimal style, no gradients, no text, rounded-square iOS icon format, 1024x1024.
styles.promptHint: Keep stroke weight above 1/40 of the canvas width or it breaks at small sizes; if the glyph is generic, add one proprietary detail (like Notion's serif foot).

styles.name: Dark Tech
styles.tagline: A cold gleam on black — engineers spot their own at a glance
styles.intro: Near-black base plus a high-contrast glyph or subtle glow: Linear, Obsidian, ChatGPT. The dark icon broke out of developer tools and is now the default skin of 'AI-native' — it assumes the user keeps dark mode on all day, and the icon is one cold gleam in the dark ocean.
why: Native to dark mode: developers and AI users live in dark UIs — no inversion needed
Cold filter: black carries a 'capabilities, not marketing' air that screens out non-target users
Glow memory: one gradient gleam is the entire decoration — restraint is the identifier
Constraint: risky for mass consumer apps — black triggers 'professional software anxiety'

cases.note: Concentric colored arcs on near-black — 'Linear aesthetics' has become the name of a design school.
A glowing crystal on deep purple: the knowledge tool carves the 'mined ore' metaphor right into the icon.
A white knot-flower on black — the most imitated silhouette of the AI era.

styles.prompt: Design an app icon for {{APP_NAME}}: near-black background (#0B0B0F), a single minimal glyph of {{SUBJECT}} in white or a subtle {{COLOR_1}} glow gradient, thin precise strokes, dark-mode native, no text, no drop shadow, rounded-square iOS icon format, 1024x1024.
styles.promptHint: One glow color, one direction only; also export a pure-white inverted variant for light contexts.
